entry_mode_text: Buy limit at 7394.69 (daily P + 0.10 x (daily R1 - daily P)). Reference close 7409.80 (2026-05-12 cash session); signed gap entry - reference close = -15.11 pts, i.e. the order rests below the reference close, which is the side a BUY LIMIT must sit on. It is not a buy stop: 7394.69 is below the reference close on both the cash basis (7409.80) and the full broker-day basis (7402.00), so a stop label would be on the wrong side. Order is live from the 09:00 broker anchor and fills on first touch.
management_text: Three equal units. Unit 1 exits at TP1 7435.10 (daily R1). Unit 2 exits at TP2 7447.75 (daily R1.5). On the Unit 2 fill, the Unit 3 stop moves to entry + 0.2R = 7399.64. Unit 3 runs to TP3 7460.40 (daily R2) and traces the structure; no session-close time stop is imposed by the branch rule. Thesis invalidation, distinct from the stop: a daily close back through the daily pivot 7390.20 (invalidation sits 20.24 pts above the stop, far more than 0.15 x ATR14 = 10.10, and the card therefore carries the 'stop ahead of invalidation' note).
rationale: REGIME AND BRANCH. The report's §8 short-term regime is TRANSITIONAL and its own Trade 3 fork is 3C, which under M5 §5.3 can only be selected by regime_label = TRANSITION. The branch is therefore M5 §5.2c (TRANSITION, breakout side only, aligned with the 3C upside), not the '§5.2b TREND branch' the report's card claims. §5.2c mirrors §5.2b numerically on the upside, so R1/R1.5/R2 are the target ladder. The counter-side (sell limit at R1) is not permitted under §5.2c and is not built. REFERENCE CLOSE. 7409.80, session 2026-05-12 - the settled cash-session close (16:30-23:00 broker) of the last completed session strictly before D, read from data/slices/US500/US500_upto_2026-05-12.csv. Full broker-day close of the same session, 7402.00, is quoted alongside it; every order-side test below passes on both. ATR14. 67.35 index points, 14-session window ending 2026-05-12, computed on cash-session bars (the basis the report declares in §2). The same window on full broker-day bars is 76.55; that is the figure engine/linter.py computes, so both are shown and every ATR-multiple test below is stated against both. The report never printed ATR(14) as a number at all, and the ~60 implied by its '3.5 x ATR(14) ~ 210 pts' is not used here. DAILY PIVOTS. Floor-trader formula on the D-1 CASH session H/L/C of 2026-05-12 = 7415.5 / 7345.3 / 7409.8: P = (H+L+C)/3 = 22170.6/3 = 7390.20; R1 = 2P - L = 14780.40 - 7345.30 = 7435.10; S1 = 2P - H = 14780.40 - 7415.50 = 7364.90; R2 = P + (H - L) = 7390.20 + 70.20 = 7460.40. R1.5 = (R1 + R2)/2 = 7447.75 (the M5 §4a midpoint). Identity check: R2 - P = P - S2 = 70.20 = H - L, holds. These are NOT the report's §11 daily pivots (P 7380.83 / R1 7423.12 / S1 7358.66): the report's H and C for 12 May (7403.00 and 7400.96) sit 12.5 and 8.8 pts below the slice's cash H 7415.5 and C 7409.8, so its whole pivot grid is displaced ~6 to 12 pts low. The slice is authoritative here, and this is the disagreement that moves every level on this card. ENTRY. §5.2b/§5.2c: P + 0.10 x (R1 - P) = 7390.20 + 0.10 x 44.90 = 7394.69. STOP. §5.2b primary: P - 0.8 x (P - S1) = 7390.20 - 0.8 x 25.30 = 7390.20 - 20.24 = 7369.96. The alternative anchor in the same rule ('just below S1 minus 0.25 x ATR14' where a confluence sits just below S1) would give 7364.90 - 16.84 = 7348.06 on the cash ATR, or 7345.76 on the full-day ATR, either of which is near the 12 May cash low 7345.3; the rule says take whichever is TIGHTER, and 7369.96 is tighter, so the primary formula wins. R = 7394.69 - 7369.96 = 24.73 pts = 0.37 x ATR14(cash 67.35) = 0.32 x ATR14(full-day 76.55). Both ratios are inside the mandatory 0.30-3.00 band (floors 20.21 and 22.97 pts; ceilings 202.05 and 229.65), so this clears the WARN_R_TINY that the original card took at 0.29 x ATR. R is below 1.00 x ATR14, so no 'wide stop' flag. TARGETS. TP1 = daily R1 = 7435.10 (40.41 pts from entry = 0.60 x ATR cash / 0.53 x ATR full-day, well inside the 2.5 x ATR reach of 168.38 / 191.38). TP2 = daily R1.5 = 7447.75. TP3 = daily R2 = 7460.40. No '+1R / +2R' labels are attached: on the TRANSITION/TREND branch the ladder is R1/R1.5/R2 and these distances are 1.63R / 2.15R / 2.66R, not 1R/2R. Ladder ordering: 7369.96 < 7394.69 < 7435.10 < 7447.75 < 7460.40, strictly increasing for a long. SWINGS AND FIBS. No swing anchor and no fib retracement percentage enters this card - the §5.2 pivot branch is built entirely from the daily floor-pivot grid. Swings are recorded only as confluence context: 5-day swing high 7435.00 (2026-05-11) sits exactly on TP1 daily R1, a two-way confluence inside 0.15 x ATR14, and 5-day swing low 7306.90 (2026-05-06) and 25-day swing low 6742.30 (2026-04-08) are both far below the stop. ANCHOR. 09:00 broker = the report's stated 07:00 UK daily-open anchor (broker is UTC+3, UK is BST/UTC+1, so broker = UK + 2). Neither 02:00 nor 16:30 is argued for by the report: it fixes one daily-open anchor at 07:00 UK in its header and §20, and the entry is a resting limit rather than a US-cash-open decision, so the anchor is left at the report's own value. LINTER. CLEAN, 0 DUD, 0 WARN.

REFERENCE CLOSE. 7409.80, session 2026-05-12, cash session 16:30-23:00 broker from data/slices/US500/US500_upto_2026-05-12.csv; full broker-day close of the same session 7402.00. ATR14 = 67.35 pts on cash-session bars, 14 sessions ending 2026-05-12; 76.55 on full broker-day bars (the linter's basis). RANGE. §5.3c takes the range from the 25-day swings, not the 5-day: swing_high_25d = 7435.00 printed 2026-05-11, swing_low_25d = 6742.30 printed 2026-04-08, width = 692.70, midpoint = 6742.30 + 0.50 x 692.70 = 7088.65. The original card used the 5-day swing high (the report's 7428.97 ATH) as the boundary, which is the wrong anchor for this variant, and in the slice the 11 May cash high is 7435.00 rather than 7428.97. REASON 1 - NO CONFIRMED BREAK. §4d requires a daily close beyond the boundary by at least 0.25 x ATR14: threshold = 7435.00 + 0.25 x 67.35 = 7451.84 (cash basis), or 7435.00 + 0.25 x 76.55 = 7454.14 (full-day basis). The D-1 close is 7409.80 cash / 7402.00 full-day - 42.0 / 52.1 pts short of the cash threshold. Not one close in the 25-session window clears the boundary at all, let alone by the buffer. A stop entry a few points above the high is not a substitute for the confirming close; the rule is a close test. REASON 2 - THE VARIANT CANNOT BE BUILT INSIDE THE R BAND EVEN IF IT ARMED. §5.3c fixes the stop at range_low + 0.40 x width = 6742.30 + 0.40 x 692.70 = 7019.38. Against any entry at or just above the 7435.00 boundary that is R = at least 415.6 pts = 6.17 x ATR14(cash) / 5.43 x ATR14(full-day), against a hard ceiling of 3.00 x ATR14 (202.05 / 229.65 pts). The card would be rebuilt, not warned - and there is no legal rebuild, because the stop is formula-fixed. Suppression is the only compliant outcome on this date and it does not depend on which ATR basis is chosen. The original card's stop 7335.00 ('below the 12 May low with buffer', R 97) is off-rule, and the '3.5 x ATR cap' it cited is the Trade 1 stop-cap rule, not a 3C rule. WHAT THE LADDER WOULD HAVE BEEN. Recorded only to show it was tested, not emitted: TP1 = broken high + 1.0 x width = 7435.00 + 692.70 = 8127.70; TP2 = 1.5 x measured move = 7435.00 + 1039.05 = 8474.05; TP3 = discretionary trail beyond 1.5 x MM, or null. The original card's 1R/2R ladder (7529 / 7626) is the Trade 1 geometry and its TP3 7606 sat below its own TP2, which is the WARN_TP3_ORDER the QA lint recorded. No fib retracement percentage enters a 3C card - the geometry is range-width based, and the fib swing anchor is a 3A/3B input only. INVALIDATION under §5.3c would have been a daily close back inside the range past the midpoint 7088.65, not the report's 'close below 7388'. ANCHOR. 09:00 broker = the report's 07:00 UK daily-open anchor (broker = UK + 2 in BST); stated on the suppressed row so all three cards read the same anchor. Linter: SUPPRESSED, 0 DUD.
